facts.statement: Lophorhothon is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous of Alabama, and possibly Georgia and North Carolina.
facts.quote: Lophorhothon is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Alabama, and possibly Georgia and North Carolina.

facts.statement: Remains of Lophorhothon were first discovered during the 1940s.
facts.quote: Remains of a small, poorly known perhaps saurolophine dinosaur were first discovered during the 1940s

facts.statement: The genus Lophorhothon was named by Wann Langston in 1960.
facts.quote: The genus was named by Wann Langston in 1960.

facts.statement: The name Lophorhothon means "crested nose", derived from Greek words for crested and nose.
facts.quote: The name Lophorhothon means "crested nose" (Greek lophos meaning 'crested' and rhothon meaning 'nose').

facts.statement: The juvenile holotype specimen is estimated to be 4.5 meters long, which is small for a hadrosaur.
facts.quote: The length of the holotype specimen has been estimated as 4.5 m, which is small for a hadrosaur, but the original specimen is of a juvenile.

facts.statement: Adult Lophorhothon are estimated to have been as large as Hadrosaurus, Hypsibema, Kritosaurus, and Gryposaurus.
facts.quote: The adults may have been larger, probably as large as Hadrosaurus, Hypsibema, Kritosaurus, and Gryposaurus.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was likely transported by a river and buried in silty carbonate sediments of the Mississippi embayment.
facts.quote: The specimen was likely washed out to sea by a river, where it eventually sank and was buried in the silty carbonate sediments of the Mississippi embayment.

facts.statement: A more complete specimen of Lophorhothon was unearthed in Alabama in 2021.
facts.quote: In 2021, a more complete specimen was unearthed in Alabama.

facts.statement: Some researchers have suggested that the material may represent a juvenile Prosaurolophus.
facts.quote: It has been suggested, for example, that the material may actually represent a juvenile Prosaurolophus.

facts.statement: In 1998, James Lamb suggested the genus might represent a basal iguanodont, an idea that did not gain widespread acceptance.
facts.quote: James Lamb in 1998 has suggested the genus may actually represent a basal iguanodont, an idea that has failed to find widespread acceptance.

facts.statement: A 2010 analysis indicated Lophorhothon was a basal member of the Hadrosauroidea.
facts.quote: An analysis published in 2010 indicated it was a basal member of the Hadrosauroidea.

facts.statement: Lophorhothon lived from the Santonian to the Campanian stages, approximately 85.7 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Campanian (85.7 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The name Lophorhothon means "crested nose", with the Greek roots lophos (crested) and rhothon (nose).
facts.quote: El nombre Lophorhothon significa "nariz con cresta", lophos del griego que significa "crestado" y rhothon que significa "nariz".

facts.statement: The specific name atopus is derived from the Greek word atopos, meaning "uncommon" or "strange".
facts.quote: El nombre específico se deriva del griego atopos, "poco común" o "extraño".

facts.statement: Lophorhothon is classified within the family Hadrosauridae.
Lophorhothon is classified within the subfamily Saurolophinae.
Lophorhothon lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico en el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

rejected.statement: Lophorhothon was the first dinosaur genus discovered in Alabama, United States.
rejected.quote: It was the first dinosaur genus discovered in Alabama, in the United States.
rejected.reason: quote not found verbatim in the source

rejected.statement: The holotype specimen consists of a fragmentary, disarticulated skull and an incomplete postcranial skeleton.
rejected.quote: The holotype... consists of a fragmentary and disarticulated skull and incomplete postcranial skeleton.
rejected.reason: quote not found verbatim in the source

rejected.statement: Preserved cranial material includes a partial quadrate, maxilla, teeth, jugal, lacrimal, nasal crest, postorbital, frontal, prefrontal, parietal, squamosal, paroccipital process, and a portion of the predentary bone.
rejected.quote: Preserved cranial material includes a partial quadrate, left maxilla, teeth, jugal, lacrimal, nasal (with the namesake crest), postorbital, frontal, prefrontal, parietal, squamosal, and paroccipital process and a portion of the predentary bone.

rejected.statement: Recent workers classified Lophorhothon as a basal hadrosaurine and a sister taxon to all other hadrosaurines.
rejected.quote: More recent workers (Horner, Weishampel, and Forster, 2004) have classified Lophorhothon as a basal hadrosaurine and a sister taxon to all other hadrosaurines.

rejected.statement: New material unearthed in 2021 cemented Lophorhothon's status as a valid genus of hadrosauromorph.
rejected.quote: This find cemented its status as a valid genus of hadrosauromorph.
